World.title: ‘Grain’ revolution: How lost varieties of rice are coming back
World.content:
Biryani made with Kaima instead of Basmati, payesh made with Badshahbhog, risotto made with Assamâs Bora. With heirloom rice vanishing from Indian kitchens faster than they could be documented, this seemed, until not very long ago, nothing more than nostalgia.

The Green Revolutionâs push for high-yield monoculture had, over the years, pushed out many old types of rice. But now, several of those varieties, thought long gone, are staging a comeback â thanks to the efforts of farmers, conservationists, NGOs, restaurateurs, and a bit of help from some state govts.

Guardians of the grain

In coastal Karnatakaâs Nettanige village, Padma Shri awardee Sathyanarayana Beleri â everyone calls him âSeeding Sathyaâ â nurtures more than 100 traditional paddy varieties in grow bags outside his house.

Itâs a small selection from his vast collection of over 650 seed varieties, collected from across India, Sri Lanka, Japan and the Philippines.

He has strains of flood-resistant Edekunhi and Nereguli, the medicinal Dodda Byra Nellu, and Kalanamak (also called âBuddha Riceâ). Heâs distributed seeds to hundreds of farmers across Karnataka and Kerala, as well as to agricultural universities nationwide. âRiceâ, he says, âcan be cultivated in grow bags, just like vegetables at home.





As climate change reshapes agriculture, conserving traditional, climate-resilient varieties is no longer a choice.

It is a necessity.â

Sathyanarayana Beleri with some of the more than 650 seed varieties he has collected from across India, Sri Lanka, Japan and the Philippines.

Further inland, entire families have turned conservation into a generational commitment. In Belthangady taluk, the Rao family has conserved 180-190 traditional varieties on 5.5 acres since B K Deva Rao started a seed bank in 1988. His son, Parameshwar Rao, points to a benefit beyond biodiversity.

âPaddy cultivation is among the best forms of groundwater recharge and rainwater harvesting,â he says. âStrong field bunds can retain water for nearly a week.

Even two cropping cycles can substantially improve the groundwater table.â Their prized variety, Kayame â a red rice â âhas a flavour rarely found in modern commercial varieties,â he adds.

Some 1,300km away in Chhattisgarh, Khemlal Dewangan, a maths teacher in Rajnandgaon district, started farming traditional paddy around 15 years ago.

Dewangan started with a handful of desi strains. He now has a collection of around 70 varieties.

His seed collection has grown through a nationwide network of farmers â brought together on WhatsApp â who test small quantities in their fields. âI now receive 10-15 enquiries a day from social media and word of mouth,â he says.

For him, the appeal goes beyond the market: he says traditional varieties are healthier, as they take longer to mature, absorbing more soil nutrients.

Roots of a revival

None of this happened by accident. Back in 2004, the UNâs second International Year of Rice, Kerala-based NGO Thanal decided something had to be done about Indiaâs vanishing rice varieties. They launched the Save Our Rice campaign through a workshop in Kumbalangi village. Thanal teamed up with Tamil Naduâs CREATE (a non-profit organisation) to run it, and the campaign took root in Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka and Bengal, later spreading into Chhattisgarh.

Members of CREATE educate farmers about heirloom rice varieties on a farm in Tamil Nadu.

India had over one lakh varieties of rice in 1966, but by the time the campaign started, that number had dropped to around 30,000 â most locked away in university seed banks, rather than growing in farmersâ fields. The campaign has had a big impact on southern states. âIn the last 15-16 years, there has been a revival of traditional seeds in these states,â says Jayakumar C, executive director at Thanal. âToday, there are more than 25 or 30 farmers or groups doing traditional seeds in different parts of Kerala.

Thanalâs own centre in Wayanad now holds around 320- 330 varieties of rice.â

That demand has started showing up in the market. Thanal runs a regular shop now in Thiruvananthapuram. Jayakumar says Kaima (also called Jeerakasala or Jeeraga Samba), a traditional variety, has become popular for biryani. Brands have caught on, too. Thondi, from a Wayanad farmer-producer company, sells online and via courier across Keralaâs cities, even as Mappila Chamba has built a following.

âTraditional rice tends to be more filling,â says Jayakumar. You feel full after eating less, unlike white rice hybrids. Also, the longer shelf life and taste after cooking is winning over urban households, especially the older people.â

When state stepped in

In Tamil Nadu, govt push gave the revival momentum. According to Suresh Kanna, project director at CREATE Trust, state govt began promoting six native varieties some 10 years ago under the State Heritage Rice Mission: Mappillai Samba, Karuppu Kavuni, Thooyamalli, Poongar, Kaattuyaanam and Kichili Samba.

âToday, they are liked by consumers and can be seen in organic shops across the state. They also fetch good income for the farmers.

A Kavuni farmer can get up to Rs 200 for a kilo. My calculation is that more than one lakh farmers in the state are now cultivating traditional paddy varieties,â Kanna says.

Even in Karnataka, grassroots efforts are now finding institutional backing. KVK Dakshina Kannada has begun field trials of 10 traditional varieties sourced from Beleri, aiming to identify strains suited to the coastal region, and reintroduce them into local food systems.

Karnatakaâs agriculture department has documented 2,164 traditional landraces (local, traditional varieties that evolved through natural and human selection to adapt to a specific geographic and climatic environment) across 20 crops, with paddy topping the list at 1,469 varieties, under its Conservation and Promotion of Landraces Programme.

Rs 1.3 crore in incentives went to 490 farmers in 2025-26 for viable seed samples.

The effort centres on custodian farmers who âcontinued cultivating them on small patches of land,â as department director GT Puthra puts it.

The department is now supporting GI registration for varieties including Kagga paddy, Rajmudi paddy, Bijapur Jola, Joni Bella and Kumbi Mudli, and plans incentives for 15 âforgotten treasureâ shops.

Farm to fork, fork to fame

A few restaurants are actively championing rare, indigenous rice over commercial varieties.

Edible Archives in Goa works with regional grains like Thavala Kannan from Wayanad (a red rice from Palakkad, whose name means âfrogâs eyesâ in Malayalam), and Pokkali, which brings a distinct coastal terroir.

The Kolkata-based Amar Khamar, both a heritage-grain retail brand and restaurant, is entirely built around Bengalâs native rice. Its signature is âChhuti-r Bhatâ, an 11-course meal following the traditional sequence of a Bengali meal, centred on heirloom varieties like Sugondhi Chine Kamini Aatap.

âChhuti-r Bhatâ in Kolkataâs Amar Khamar, which is an 11-course meal centred on heirloom rice varieties.

That influence has spread to other restaurants in the city. Sienna Cafe sources Chine Kamini, Radha Tilok, Kanakchur and Tulaipanji Atop from Amar Khamar; Yokocho, a Japanese alleyway-inspired bar and BBQ, draws on Kanakchur, Tulaipanji Atop and Karpurkanti; Red Bari incorporates Shatia, Mallifulo and Khejur Chhari.

Juhi Punwani, head of kitchen operations at Amar Khamar, has built a career around collecting the many myths and stories behind Bengalâs native rice varieties.

âGobindobhog is not the only heritage rice in Bengal,â she says. A rice called Radhuni Pagol literally means âthe cook gone crazyâ, after lore that its fragrance once filled a kitchen so completely that the cook couldnât think of anything else.

Tulaipanji of North Bengal gets its name from how the cooked rice turns light and airy like cotton (tula); Khejur Chhari is named for the date palm its grains resemble; Radha Tilokâs dark-tipped grain evokes Radhaâs tilak mark.

âEvery rice here has a beautiful story and a journey, and thatâs what weâre trying to showcase,â says Punwani, whose team has worked to bring back over 100 varieties, keeping around 50 in active rotation.

A look at select traditional rice varieties and the regions they are associated with across India.

This past summer, that ambition crossed continents, as Amar Khamar toured France and Germany. In Paris, working with sommelier Rajat Parr, the team built an 80-guest, 10-course tasting menu entirely around rice.

Kanakchur turned up as fritters with brown butter hollandaise, Sundarbansgrown Karpurkanti and Chine Kamini appeared as aatapan alongside a jackfruit-seed mung dal, Barddhamanâs Mohansal was served boiled, the meal closing with a Jhargram Fine Black Rice phirni.

In Stuttgart, the team built a fully vegan Bengali tasting menu, rice carrying the meal from a humble jhal muri to a coconut-milk Badshahbhog payesh for dessert.

A separate 200-guest winery event tested whether the format could scale â from Karpurkanti-paired lentils, a Chine Kamini peas pulao to Sunday lamb curry and Badshahbhog milk-rice. âNone of this would be possible without the relationships we have built with a network of farmers,â says Punwani, who executed the menu in Europe.

The traceability problem

But as heritage rice travels from the farm into retail shelves, a different problem emerges: knowing whether whatâs being sold is really what it claims to be.

One store has built its entire business around solving exactly that. In Chennaiâs Mylapore sits a store unlike any other. Spirit of the Earth calls itself a âretail store and experience centreâ, where customers come to see, touch, feel and know the story of every rice.

Opened in 2017, itâs the retail face of a project that Sheela Balaji, chairperson of NGO AIM For Seva, began over a decade ago, built on a principle she believes the heritage-rice surge often misses: traceability.

âUnfortunately, certain grains are being sold as certain varieties, which is inaccurate,â says Balaji.

âThe minute you say heritage rice, people will just come and buy it. But who is taking accountability? How do you know if itâs really diabetic friendly? So, I started this project more than a decade ago, first and foremost by building a seed bank. All the rice that you see in our store is grown from our farm in Manjakkudi, a village in Tiruvarur.â

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The 40-acre operation has grown as neighbouring farmers joined in, alongside a seed bank built from years of Balajiâs fieldwork with growers in Manipur, Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh.

For Balaji, the mission is beyond nutrition or nostalgia. âRice in our culture is Lakshmi,â she says. âAnd reintroducing its forgotten names and forms, one customer at a time, is as much about restoring that reverence as it is about the grain itself.â

World.title: Ajit Doval’s China visit: NSA, Chinese VP Han Zheng discuss border peace, bilateral ties
World.content:
NEW DELHI: National security advisor

on Tuesday met Chinese vice president Han Zheng in Beijing, with the two sides discussing ways to maintain peace and tranquillity along the border and further strengthen India-China relations across economic, political and multilateral platforms.

The meeting came ahead of the 25th round of special representatives talks on the India-China boundary question between Doval and Chinese foreign minister Wang Yi later on Tuesday.

Sharing details of the meeting, the Embassy of India in China said, "On 25 August, NSA and Special Representative on the India-China Boundary Question, Ajit Doval called on Han Zheng, Vice President of the People's Republic of China."

The embassy said Doval and Han discussed ways to strengthen peace and tranquillity in the border areas and further improve bilateral ties "across economic, political and multilateral fora", in line with the consensus reached by the leaders of the two countries.

Doval arrived in Beijing on Monday for a two-day visit to participate in the Special Representatives talks with Wang Yi, who is also China's Foreign Minister.

The talks are expected to focus on the boundary question, along with bilateral, regional and international issues.

The Chinese Foreign Ministry has described the Special Representatives mechanism as the "main channel" for negotiations between the two countries on the boundary question and an important platform for communication on issues of mutual interest.





The mechanism was established in 2003 to address the India-China boundary dispute, which stretches across roughly 3,488 km.

The 24th round of talks was held in August last year, when the two sides held what Beijing described as candid and in-depth discussions and reached several common understandings.

The upcoming round assumes significance as India and China seek to stabilise ties following years of tensions along the Line of Actual Control.

The discussions come amid efforts by New Delhi and Beijing to gradually improve bilateral relations after the 2020 Galwan Valley clash and the prolonged military stand-off in eastern Ladakh severely strained ties.

Doval and Wang had also met in June in New Delhi on the sidelines of the BRICS National Security Advisers' meeting. The Ministry of External Affairs had described those discussions as "constructive and forward-looking".

MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal had said, "The two sides reviewed recent developments in bilateral relations and noted progress towards gradual normalisation. NSA underlined that stable, predictable and constructive bilateral relations contribute to building trust and better understanding between the two sides. The discussions were constructive and forward-looking."

The latest talks also come amid efforts by the two countries to build on a series of high-level engagements between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping.

The leaders had welcomed positive momentum and steady progress in bilateral relations during their meeting on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Tianjin last year, after their previous meeting in Kazan in October 2024.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

They had reaffirmed that India and China are development partners rather than rivals and that differences should not be allowed to become disputes.

"A stable relationship and cooperation between India and China and their 2.8 billion peoples on the basis of mutual respect, mutual interest and mutual sensitivity are necessary for the growth and development of the two countries, as well as for a multipolar world and a multi-polar Asia befitting the trends of the 21st century," the MEA had said after the leaders' meeting.

Despite the gradual improvement in ties, differences over the boundary and Arunachal Pradesh remain sensitive issues between New Delhi and Beijing.

Both Doval and Wang are designated Special Representatives for the boundary talks mechanism. While the process has not resolved the long-running border dispute, officials on both sides continue to regard it as an important channel for managing tensions and maintaining communication.

The talks also come ahead of Xi's expected visit to New Delhi for the BRICS summit on September 12-13, which could provide an opportunity for another meeting between Xi and PM Modi and further discussions on the bilateral relationship.

World.title: Prevent misuse of data by private entities, SC tells government
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Monday expressed concern about a commercial technological ecosystem which allegedly accesses, retrieves and verifies sensitive individual information on provident fund and income tax returns and told the Centre about the desirability of devising an antidote to the problem with the assistance of domain experts.

Hearing a PIL by Piyush Sharma, a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana noted the matter essentially fell within policy domain but termed private access to sovereign data - individual information given to govt under legislative mandate - and its commercial exploitation as worrisome.

Petitioner said his personal inquiry into the issue had revealed that "upon merely furnishing PAN and UAN details to a private verification workflow, the petitioner received complete employment history corresponding the said identifiers.

No OTP authentication was generated. No explicit consent was obtained. No visible authorisation-based identity verification process was undertaken".

Without blaming govt agencies for any leakage of data, the petitioner highlighted the insecure status of individual data given to govt under the mandate of different laws, as they are accessed at will by private entities.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

"Despite the statutory architecture governing EPFO and I-T data, there appears to be an emerging and concerning pattern wherein private employment verification ecosystems rely upon data corresponding to statutory employment and financial records for purposes such as employment verification, moonlighting detection, dual employment screening, labour market profiling and employment decision-making," he said.





SC agreed it was a serious matter but said it must be dealt with through a policy decision. On learning the petitioner sent two comprehensive representations on the issues to Centre, it asked govt to take "necessary steps to prevent misuse of individual data by private enterprises."

World.title: Delhi protest crackdown: Supreme Court says right to peaceful protest constitutionally protected, mulls framing guidelines
World.content:
The Supreme Court on Monday (July 27, 2026) observed that the constitutional right to peaceful protest must be protected and indicated that it may consider framing uniform guidelines to regulate police conduct during large-scale demonstrations.

A Bench led by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant said it was equally concerned about injuries suffered by both protesters and police personnel during such protests, and stressed that “self-imposed discipline” on the part of both citizens and law enforcement was essential to the functioning of a democracy.

NEET-UG protests case: Petitioners seek re-constitution of high-powered enquiry committee

“The right to peaceful protest is absolutely guaranteed under the Constitution. So long as it is a peaceful agitation, merely because there is agitation, there cannot be [police excesses]... If there is police excess committed, it should be independently examined. Merely because there is agitation, it does not mean there should be a lathi charge. Discipline is integral to the democratic process,” the Chief Justice orally remarked.

The oral observations came as multiple petitions concerning the nationwide protests over examination paper leaks were mentioned before the Bench, which also comprised Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana. These included petitions alleging police excesses during the July 20 Parliament march led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), as well as those concerning the alleged “aerial firing” by police personnel in Bihar’s Siwan during the Bihar bandh on Saturday (July 25, 2026), called by the All India Students’ Association (AISA) over the NEET paper leak.

Following the protests, which spread across several States and snowballed into a major political crisis for the Narendra Modi government, Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as the Union Education Minister on Saturday (July 25, 2026). Union Minister Pralhad Joshi assumed charge as the new Education Minister on Sunday (July 26, 2026). Meanwhile, in a move to strengthen the anti-cheating law, the Union government proposed the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, which seeks to increase the punishment for those involved in unfair means, including the leaking of question papers for public examinations, from three to five years’ imprisonment to five to 10 years. It also proposes to enhance the maximum fine from ₹10 lakh to ₹50 lakh. A copy of the Bill was circulated among Members of Parliament on Saturday.

Mentioning one of the petitions for urgent listing, advocate Fauzia Shakil, appearing for Rajya Sabha member Manoj Jha, told the court that a comprehensive writ petition had been filed placing on record material relating to the police action, including the alleged firing on protesters in Bihar’s Siwan district.

“We have filed a writ petition with comprehensive information, including Bihar firing... There was use of AK-47 in Siwan... we have filed data,” Ms. Shakil submitted.

The Chief Justice said the court was already seized of a petition seeking all-India guidelines to regulate protests. “There is a petition seeking all-India guidelines for protests etc. There is a right to peaceful protest. It is allowed,” he remarked, after senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for petitioner-advocate Shailesh Mani Tripathi, submitted that his plea presses for such guidelines.

‘Police literally lynched’

On Monday (July 27, 2026), senior advocate Sreedhar Pottaraju brought to the notice of the Bench that a petition had been filed on behalf of the families of police personnel allegedly assaulted during the July 20 Parliament march. Seeking to intervene in the proceedings, he submitted, “I represent the families of policemen who have been brutally beaten. We would like to participate, My Lords, and present our perspective. Protect the police as well in uniform.”

Mr. Pottaraju added that while there was “no question of defending excesses”, the rights of police personnel in uniform also deserved protection. “There are videos circulating. They have been kicked, literally lynched,” he submitted.

Responding to the submission, Justice Bagchi said the court’s concern extended equally to the injuries allegedly suffered by police personnel. He observed that the state authorities would be called upon to explain whether adequate protective gear and safety equipment had been provided to officers deployed to manage large crowds.

“Injuries to all individuals, be it policemen or anyone else, are of equal concern to us. We may call upon the state to explain why adequate safety gear, guards, helmets etc. were not provided to police personnel,” the Judge remarked.

‘Uniform protocol’

Senior advocate Vikas Singh urged the court to frame uniform guidelines governing police action during protests, pointing out that allegations of police excesses were not confined to Delhi but had surfaced across the country. “There have to be pan-India guidelines and some kind of balancing,” he said.

The Chief Justice agreed that a standard operating protocol appeared necessary. “There has to be a protocol in place. Everyone has a right to protest so long as it is with due permission and at designated places. But if some anti-social elements have done anything, that can also be looked into,” he remarked.

Pleas to be heard on July 28

Noting that the issues raised extended beyond any single State, the CJI said all pending petitions would be heard together on Tuesday (July 28, 2026). He also assuaged the petitioners, saying that the court would examine allegations of disproportionate use of force by the police as well as incidents of violence during the protests.

“We will list all the matters tomorrow. Do not take it adversely. If there are excesses committed, that can be looked into dispassionately... who has done it, etc. It can also not be that violence occurs during these protests”, CJI Kant said.

Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Delhi Police, said the police had no objection to all the petitions being heard together. “We are not taking it adversely. Let all the matters be taken up together,” he submitted.

The Bench thereafter directed that all pending petitions be listed together for hearing on Tuesday (July 28, 2026).

On July 24, 2026, the apex court had agreed to hear on Monday two freshly instituted petitions alleging police excesses during the July 20 crackdown on student protesters in the national capital. The development came hours after the Chief Justice clarified in open court that “no petition” had previously been filed on the issue and criticised “reckless” reports suggesting that the court had refused to list such a matter.

The observations came two days after the court declined to initiate suo motu proceedings on an oral request made by advocate Narendra Mishra to take cognisance of the alleged police brutality during the July 20 Parliament march organised by the CJP.

Ban use of pellet guns for crowd control’

On Monday, retired Intelligence Bureau Special Director Yashovardhan Azad, along with two other victims of alleged pellet-gun injuries, an artist and another professional, moved the Supreme Court seeking a ban on the use of wholly or partly metallic kinetic projectiles fired from pump-action or projectile-action guns (PAG) for crowd control by law enforcement agencies. The petition also seeks exemplary compensation for all those allegedly injured by pellet firing during the July 20 protests, besides directions to ensure their complete medical treatment, rehabilitation and long-term care.

“The use of such projectile-action guns (PAGs) or pellet guns loaded with wholly or partly metallic pellets for crowd dispersal fails the constitutional tests of necessity, proportionality and reasonableness. It amounts to an unconstitutional fetter on the right to freedom of assembly guaranteed under Article 19(1)(b) of the Constitution. The petitioners, therefore, pray that such weapons be decommissioned or banned from being deployed for crowd dispersal against civilian assemblies,” the plea states.

The petition comes days after The Hindu reported that two unarmed protesters were struck by pellets allegedly fired by personnel of the Rapid Action Force (RAF). Following the report, the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) said on Friday (July 24, 2026) that it was “verifying the media reports”. A CRPF official said no action had been initiated as the force was still ascertaining the veracity of the allegations.

World.title: ‘Agadha’ movie review: Kamakshi Bhaskarla shines, but style outruns substance
World.content:
Barely a week after Korean Kanakaraju, a no-brainer milking the viewer’s endless appetite for horror comedies, Telugu cinema’s tryst with ghosts, evil spirits and tantric practices continues with Agadha, set to a different metre. It is a primitive yet visually arresting good-versus-evil supernatural thriller that takes itself quite seriously.

Agadha arrives with an underdog advantage. One does not expect much, going by director MS Raju’s modest track record. In this film, he has banked on a young team to deliver the goods. On the surface, it has the staple ingredients of a rustic horror tale, with occult rituals, hymns, long-bearded sages and even older belief systems, but it is staged with flair.

Mahadevi (Kamakshi Bhaskarla) is a yogini, a glorified exorcist who returns to her ancestral home when an evil spirit torments her family. A series of creepy events in the household follows the death of a pregnant woman. The misfortune is traced back to an adventure trip to Chhattisgarh’s Bastar, where three friends enter a haunted cave and encounter a religious cult.

Agadha (Telugu) Director: M.S. Raju Cast: Kamakshi Bhaskarla, Shravan Reddy, Ulka Gupta Runtime: 137 minutes Storyline: An exorcist returns home to guard her family tormented by an evil spirit

A bizarre early sequence has Mahadevi claiming that a dead woman continues to be a restless soul because her grandson has kept her dentures. That far-fetched lore, coupled with Mahadevi’s backstory of a carefree girl suddenly entrusted with a divine purpose and a shaky family dynamic, consumes considerable screen time and stalls the early momentum.

Every second sequence, aided by the music, visuals and locales, teases viewers with the hope of delivering something more than the obvious. While the technical crew appears ready to push the bar despite the limitations, and Kamakshi is at home shouldering the proceedings, the writing does not complement their efforts. It remains intriguing in atmosphere, yet leaves me craving more.

Post-intermission, style is backed by substance with greater consistency. Agadha’s (the evil force) crooked tactics to gain control over the universe are laid bare in arresting detail. Agadha and Mahadevi throw nasty challenges at one another frequently, and their tussle for supremacy is engrossing, something Rakesh Venkatapuram’s score uplifts to good effect. While the ending is anyone’s guess, its masala-laden treatment is fun to watch.

For all the agency it claims to give women, and the abundant screen time they are provided, Agadha’s female characters are either saints or victims of evil spirits. In its aim to be a layered good-versus-evil story, many characters are reduced to binaries. What about Mahadevi, the woman, beyond her role as a divine messenger? What makes Agadha so bitter? The writing fails to dig deep.

Moreover, the visual aesthetic heavily borrows from the atmosphere of the 2018 Hindi film Tumbbad, focusing on deity worship, ancient sorcery and lush green landscapes to generate an air of dread. This emphasis on visual appeal has its repercussions, mainly in its inability to generate genuine chills and maintain a strong narrative grip. The repeated use of crows as a metaphor for doom is tiresome. Yet the impressive shot composition, precise framing (cinematography by Nani Chamidisetty) and art direction (by Rajeev Nair) remain among its highlights.

Despite the unidimensional writing and the boundaries around Mahadevi’s character, Kamakshi Bhaskarla displays enough confidence in her portrayal. Shravan Reddy has the right build and body language to be a menacing baddie, but there is only so much scope the film offers him. Ulka Gupta is good while she lasts. Jovika is strictly okay in her debut, whilst her on- and off-screen mother, Vanitha Vijayakumar, lacks a meaty part. Shiju’s unusual casting in a sage-like avatar nearly pays off.

The impressive craft in Agadha is undeniable, but does that make it a genuinely satisfying, value-for-money horror film? Not quite.

World.title: Delhi Police authorised pellet gun use against protestors on July 20: RAF general diary entry
World.content:
Days after the Delhi Police denied the usage of pellet guns during the July 20 march to Parliament — in which at least four persons reported being hit with pellets — a general diary entry filed at Parliament Street police station reveals that the Rapid Action Force (RAF) did fire two rounds from an anti-riot gun on the directions of a Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) rank officer.

Also Read | 19-year-old may lose vision in right eye due to pellet injury, says family

The Hindu has accessed the general diary entry, which was registered by the RAF at 1:24 a.m. on July 22. This was the first time that a pellet gun was used against unarmed protestors in the national capital.

‘I apologised, threats did not stop’: after Jantar Mantar protest, women face doxxing, calls to 'teach them a lesson'

Following the July 20 incident, the RAF withdrew shock batons, electric shields, pump-action guns, and the anti-riot guns, which fire pellets, from personnel deployed at Jantar Mantar. A review by an RAF Inpsector General also highlighted “serious deficiencies” in RAF behaviour during the march, in violation of its principle of “sensitive policing”.

Two rounds fired

The diary entry says that, to control the crowd during the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protest, “on the orders of Zone-1, DCP, Jantar Mantar,” the RAF Deputy Commandant fired “55 rounds of non-electrical shell, 15 rounds of electrical shell, five tear smoke granite, two rounds using ballistic cartridges with plastic pellets from an anti-riot gun.” The RAF, which is the anti-riot unit of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), was deployed and was under the operational control of the Delhi Police at the time of the incident.

At least 10 people injured by pellets on July 20, shows RTI response

The diary entry was made hours after The Hindu reported on July 21 that two people allegedly hit by pellets fired by RAF personnel had undergone surgery at government hospitals. One of them, Sahil Lochab, 19, risks losing vision in his right eye due to a pellet piercing his pupil, his family said.

NEET-UG protests case: Petitioners seek re-constitution of high-powered enquiry committee

Police sources said that during a law-and-order situation, Central forces, in this case the RAF, are given a general consent by the police officer concerned, to use all crowd-control equipment at their disposal.

Rahul Gandhi sits on dharna at police station in New Delhi, demands FIR over pellet gun use during July 20 protest

‘Serious deficiencies’

Significantly, in a video conference with RAF personnel after the incident, RAF Inspector General Seema Dhundhia “gave clear directions that during the current Delhi deployment, the situation has been analysed and until further orders pump action guns (PAG), anti-riot Gun (ARG), electric shock weapon, and electric shield shall not be used or issued to personnel.”

The minutes of the review meeting accessed by The Hindu said that “serious deficiencies were observed in many aspects of the operation, which need to be improved in the future.”

The Inspector General reiterated that the core principle of the RAF is “sensitive policing”, and directed that the use of force in every situation must be done only to the necessary extent, in a judicious, fair, restrained, and sensitive manner.

‘Contrary to RAF culture’

Ms. Dhundhia said that “some videos available on social media showed incidents of RAF personnel using unnecessary force on persons who had already separated from the crowd, deliberately making people fall, and assaulting persons going out of the barricade. Such incidents are completely contrary to the established work culture and image of RAF and are not justified under any circumstances.”

She directed that, in the future, all personnel must be clearly briefed that the identity of RAF lies in disciplined, impartial, restrained, and sensitive policing, and that this standard must be strictly followed during every operation.

The I-G also asked RAF personnel to document all events. “If any personnel is injured, the availability of medical records, required documents, and FIRs registered by the concerned state police etc. must be ensured. Further, the quantum of force used by RAF, tear gas shells, other crowd control equipment, and related data must fully match with the records of the State police and FIRs. Any kind of factual discrepancy must be avoided and all records must be kept 100% accurate and complete,” she said.

Public scrutiny

Noting the prevalence of social media and mobile cameras in modern times, Ms. Dhundhia cautioned RAF personnel that every operation remains under public scrutiny. “During the observation of various videos and reels available on social media during the protest at Jantar-Mantar,it was found that several personnel were seen performing duty without body protectors and helmets, which is contrary to the prescribed standards and security-related instructions. Therefore, in the future, before every deployment, it must be ensured that all personnel are fully equipped with the prescribed protective gear,” she said.

Retired Intelligence Bureau Special Director Yashovardhan Azad moved the Supreme Court for a ban on pellet guns on July 27, along with two victims of pellet gun injuries, an artist and another professional. They demanded the decommissioning or ban on the use of wholly or partly metallic kinetic projectiles or pellets fired from pump action rifles or projectile action guns for the purpose of crowd dispersal of civilian assemblies by law enforcement agencies. They also sought the grant of exemplary compensation as well as complete medical treatment, care and rehabilitation for all victims of pellet injuries caused by the State action on July 20.

World.title: Day after Gautam Adani meets D.K. Shivakumar, Karnataka government amends two laws to clear legal hurdles for tunnel road project
World.content:
A day after Gautam Adani, chairman, Adani Group, which has emerged as the lowest bidder in Bengaluru’s North-South Twin Tunnel project, visited Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar at his residence, the Karnataka government passed Bills amending two laws in both Houses of the State legislature on Monday (August 24) to clear legal hurdles for the project.

Three PILs in the High Court of Karnataka challenging the tunnel road project had contended that the project was in violation of these two laws. The move has drawn strong condemnation from the petitioners arguing that this amounted to “regularising violations in retrospect”.

Laws amended

On Monday, the legislature passed The Bengaluru Metropolitan Land Transport Authority (Amendment) Bill, 2026, which gives deemed approval for all projects initiated after the commencement of the BMLTA Act, 2022, and before the notification of the BMLTA Rules, 2026, on July 3. A batch of three PILs in the High Court had contended that as per Section 19 of the BMLTA Act, 2022, the Authority had to approve all major urban mobility projects in Bengaluru and the tunnel road project did not have this approval. Now, as per the amendment Bill, the project will be “deemed approved”.

Satya Arikutharam, an independent urban mobility expert, said that the BMLTA Act, 2022, was passed in 2023, but the Authority was not constituted for years. “When citizens challenged the tunnel road project for not being approved by BMLTA, as per Section 19 of the BMLTA Act, 2022, the State government notified BMLTA Rules, 2026, on July 3, which comprised Rule 24 that gave deemed approval to projects prior to the notification of the rules. There are two PILs challenging the constitutionality of Rule 24, apart from the three PILs challenging tunnel roads. Fearing the court may strike down Rule 24, the government has now amended the Act itself to accord approval for all the unscientific car-centric projects,” he alleged.

Contentions about statutory non-compliance of the tunnel road project in the 3 PILs Status now Violation of Bengaluru Metropolitan Transport Authority Act, 2022, as tunnel roads project was not approved by BMLTA as per Section 19 of the Act Section 19 of the Act amended for the projects taken up between 2023 when BMLTA Act came into force and BMLTA Rules, 2026 was notified, to be “deemed approved” Tunnel Road project to take up 6 acres of Lalbagh land temporarily during construction and 1 acre permanently, in violation of Section 5 of The Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) Act, 1975 Section 5 of the Act amended allowing 5% of the park or garden lands to be alienated by means of sale, lease, gift, exchange, mortgage for “public purposes” No scrutiny of the project by Bengaluru Metropolitan Planning Committee (BMPC) violating Article 243ZE of the Constitution of India BMPC that was constituted in 2014 lapsed with the term of the then state government in 2018 and has never been reconstituted since then Project neither part of the Revised Master Plan - 2015 nor planned as a part of the master plan preparation process, violating Karnataka Town and Country Planning Act, 1961 Draft RMP-2031 was withdrawn by the state government over not being in sync with the Comprehensive Mobility Plan by BMRCL in 2020 and the Draft RMP-2041 is still in the works. The RMP-2015 which is in force in the city, doesn’t include the tunnel road project, nor was it planned as part of the exercise of drawing up RMP-2041.

Likewise, The Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) (Amendment) Bill, 2026, which allows alienation of 5% of parks and garden lands for public purposes, was also passed. The tunnel road project will need one acre of Lalbagh land, while six acres will be used temporarily for construction. The Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) Act, 1975, doesn’t allow this and the three PILs flagged the tunnel road as violating this law by taking over Lalbagh land.

Both bills were cleared by the State Cabinet on Friday and passed in both houses of the legislature on Monday, amid protests by BJP members. During the passage of the Bill, BJP and JD(S) members raised slogans such as “carpet for Adani and biscuit for Bengaluru public”, accusing the government of moving closer to Adani Group chairman Gautam Adani in connection with the tunnel project.

Petitioners condemn

N.S. Mukunda, one of the petitioners in the High Court against the tunnel road project, condemned the amendments, which he described as “an attempt to make some of their grounds infructuous in retrospect”. He said this was a “deeply undemocratic move and they will fight it in the court and also petition the Governor appealing him to not give them (the amendment Bills) his assent”.

“This is also a form of Akrama-Sakrama, which we have been fighting in the court as well. If the governments adopt this strategy, citizens can win no legal battle against it. This is perverse,” Mr. Mukunda said.

However, the three PILs have flagged other statutory non-compliances apart from these two laws, such as no approval from Bengaluru Metropolitan Planning Committee (BMPC), and the project not being part of the Revised Master Plan - 2015.

The High Court on July 16, 2026, directed that any contract for the tunnel road project will be subject to the outcome of the three PILs challenging the project. The court also said the government should inform the contractors in writing that the contract would be subject to the final outcome of the petitions. The next hearing was scheduled for August 20, but did not come up for hearing that day.

World.title: Calcutta High Court grants protection to TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee from arrest in three cases
World.content:
The Calcutta High Court on Tuesday (August 25, 2026) directed the police not to take any coercive steps against TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee in three criminal cases against him till November 30, holding that custodial interrogation is not necessary.

The court directed the Diamond Harbour MP not to travel abroad without permission of the High Court.

Justice Saugata Bhattacharyya clarified that the permission granted to Mr. Banerjee by the Supreme Court for going abroad for three weeks for medical reasons would not be curtailed by this order.

Holding that custodial interrogation of the TMC leader in connection with the three cases is not necessary, the court directed the police not to take any coercive steps against him till November 30.

Justice Bhattacharyya directed the police to file a progress report on the investigation in the three cases when the matter will be taken up for hearing again on November 23.

Mr. Banerjee was directed to cooperate with the investigation and comply with notices issued in connection with the three cases.

Justice Bhattacharyya directed that at least 48 hours’ prior notice be given to Mr. Banerjee for appearance before the investigators in the cases.

He directed that the police authorities concerned may move this court for variation or vacation of the order if Mr. Banerjee does not cooperate with the investigations.

The court also directed that Mr. Banerjee will not go abroad without permission from this court.

Mr. Banerjee's lawyer mentioned that the Supreme Court has on August 10 permitted him to travel abroad for medical reasons.

The State's lawyer submitted that the apex court order granting permission to Mr. Banerjee to travel abroad applies only to the petition that was before it.

Mr. Banerjee's lawyer stated before the court that the MP has not gone abroad yet, as he requires a doctor's appointment and also that his personal bank account and debit and credit cards were frozen by a private bank.

"The order passed today shall not in any way curtail the right of the petitioner to go abroad for treatment in terms of the order passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court on August 10, 2026, for treatment, subject to compliance of conditions mentioned in the said order," Justice Bhattacharyya clarified.

A prayer for stay of operation of this order by the additional advocate general was declined by the court.

The High Court had on June 30 granted interim protection to Banerjee from coercive steps by the police in connection with three FIRs lodged against him at Bhowanipore, Bishnupur and Kalitala police stations.

World.title: Supreme Court’s Samadhan Samaroh 2026 concludes with over 1,250 cases resolved
World.content:
The three-day Special Lok Adalat held at the Supreme Court as part of the Samadhan Samaroh 2026 concluded on August 23, with 1,712 cases settled or disposed of, according to the Supreme Court.

A total of 3,285 cases were listed during the three-day exercise. Of these, 1,664 were settled or disposed of through the Lok Adalat, while 48 cases were resolved through mediation.

The Special Lok Adalat was held from August 21 to 23 under the guidance of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant. Senior Judges, senior advocates, advocates-on-record, and other advocates were part of the Lok Adalat benches, wh were assisted by officials of the Supreme Court Registry.

The initiative, called Supreme Court Action for Mediated Adjudication and Disputes Harmonization Across Nation (SAMADHAN), began on April 21 with a pre-settlement process to identify pending cases that could be resolved amicably.

On August 21, 588 cases were listed and 402 were settled or disposed of. On August 22, 1,159 cases were listed, of which 350 were settled or disposed of. On August 23, 1,538 cases were listed and 912 were settled or disposed of.

The cases included matrimonial and property disputes, motor accident claims, land acquisition and compensation matters, tax cases, and service and labour disputes.

A total of ₹240.94 crore was settled during the three-day period. The Supreme Court said the exercise was aimed at promoting consensual dispute resolution, reducing pendency and saving judicial time in matters that could be resolved through settlement.

Cases were also disposed of amicably between April 21 and August 20 as part of the wider pre-settlement exercise.

World.title: Tamil Nadu taking steps to distribute medicine for haemophilia patients: Health Minister
World.content:
Tamil Nadu Health Minister K.G. Arunraj on Tuesday (August 25, 2026) told the Assembly that the State government was taking steps to distribute Emicizumab to patients with Haemophilia A.

Responding to a calling-attention motion moved by M.S. Ravi, who wanted the government to distribute the medicine free of cost to patients, the Minister said Emicizumab was used to treat Haemophilia A patients with Factor VIII inhibitor antibodies.

“It has not been included in the National Health Mission (NHM) essential medicines list. However, the government is taking steps to distribute the medicine to patients,” the Minister said.

World.title: NSA Doval calls on Chinese Vice-President Han Zheng ahead of border talks
World.content:
National Security Advisor Ajit Doval on Tuesday (August 25, 2026) called on Han Zheng, Vice-President of the People’s Republic of China, ahead of the 25th Round of the Special Representatives (SR) talks today.

In a post on X, the Indian Embassy in Beijing said that the “NSA and VP Han discussed ways to strengthen peace & tranquility in the border areas and further improve bilateral relations across economic, political and multilateral fora, in accordance with the consensus reached between the leaders of the two countries.”

Mr. Doval, as the Special Representative on the India-China Boundary Question, is set to meet with Politburo member and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi, his counterpart as SR later today in Beijing.

Both Mr. Doval and Mr. Wang are the designated SRs for the boundary talks mechanism, which was established in 2003 to comprehensively address the dispute of the India-China border spanning 3,488 km.

Mr. Doval’s visit comes ahead of next month’s expected trip to India by Chinese President Xi Jinping for the September 12 BRICS Summit, and provides both sides the opportunity to take stock of the relationship.

Ties have gradually normalised following the October 2024 meeting between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Mr. Xi in Kazan, Russia.

(With inputs from PTI)

World.title: Amid distrust, Tehran wants US to initiate de-escalation
World.content:
Pakistan’s Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir exchanges views with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian during their meeting in Tehran.—Reuters

• CDF Munir holds meetings with Pezeshkian, Ghalibaf and Rezaei

• Iranian leaders stress commitment to Islamabad MoU; say Washington’s approach hindering regional stability, eroding trust in US

• Discussions focused on preventing further escalation, reopening of Hormuz, swift end to conflict, ISPR says

• Oman FM due in Tehran today for next round of talks on Hormuz

ISLAMABAD: The United States must take the first steps towards de-escalation by fulfilling its commitments under the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), Iran conveyed to Pakistan on Monday, as the latter sought to revive the diplomatic process for ending the US-Iran conflict.

The message was conveyed during Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir’s meetings in Tehran; with Iranian President Dr Masoud Pezeshkian, chief negotiator and Parliament Speaker Bagher Ghalibaf, and Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council Gen Mohsen Rezaei, as he sounded out Tehran on the possibility of reviving the June understanding.

“We are committed to implementing the terms of the Memorandum of Understanding. It is the United States that must adhere to its commitments based on the agreement,” Ghalibaf told Field Marshal Munir, according to an Iranian account of their meeting.

This sentiment was echoed by Gen Rezaei in his meeting with Field Marshal Munir, who was quoted by IRNA as saying: “We distrust America and it must change its behaviour”.

Field Marshal Munir said Pakistan would continue its efforts to help restore stability in the region, Press TV reported.

According to Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi accompanied the army chief during the one-day visit, which also included meetings with Iranian Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi.

“Comprehensive discussions focused on measures to prevent further escalation, reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and expedited termination of the conflict. The two sides also exchanged views on regional peace and the ways to arrive at a negotiated settlement to the disputes,” ISPR said.

The Iranian leadership appreciated Pakistan’s constructive role and sincere efforts towards facilitating dialogue, de-escalation and a peaceful resolution of the conflict, the statement noted.

The field marshal’s visit comes as the two warring sides have returned to hostilities following the expiry of the 60-day armistice brokered under the Islamabad MoU.

Pakistan has, however, continued to regard the agreement as the available framework for a return to dialogue, while Iran has insisted that Washington must first address what Tehran considers breaches of the understanding.

The visit assumes added significance because Field Marshal Munir spoke by telephone with US President Donald Trump last week, before travelling to Tehran. The contents of that conversation have not been made public, but the contact provided Islamabad with a direct channel to carry the US position to Tehran, while seeking to assess whether Iran was prepared to re-engage.

The army chief’s trip began just before Washington announced a fresh economic pressure campaign against Iran, with sanctions and restrictions on Iranian oil exports likely to form a major part of the new measures.

Tehran has warned that further US pressure would deepen the confrontation rather than create conditions for negotiations.

Ghalibaf described Washington’s approach as “hinder[ing] regional stability and further erod[ing] trust in Washington”.

“Americans know that no one buys their bombast, the United States is not in an economic position to further restrict its relations with other countries,” he said in a post on X after meeting Field Marshal Munir.

The Strait of Hormuz remains central to the impasse. Iran has been insisting that US first fulfil its commitments relating to the waterway, before it considers a wider reopening and a return to the next phase of negotiations.

Field Marshal Munir’s meeting with Gen Rezaei was particularly significant because the Iranian general has recently taken over as secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, placing him at the centre of Tehran’s national security decision making at this critical stage in its confrontation with Washington.

During their conversation, Rezaei particularly emphasised Iran’s security interests in the Strait of Hormuz and the need for any settlement to address the military and economic pressures imposed on Tehran.

The issue of Strait of Hormuz is meanwhile being discussed in a separate diplomatic track in the shape of Iran-Oman talks on arrangements for navigation in the strait.

Omani Foreign Minister Badr Al Busaidi is due in Tehran on Tuesday, adding to the diplomatic activity surrounding the strait at a time when Pakistan is seeking to regain its role in the wider US-Iran process.

Published in Dawn, August 25th, 2026

World.title: Govt fails to maintain quorum as PPP stays away from National Assembly
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The ruling PML-N on Monday suffered an embarrassing setback in the National Assembly as the lower house was adjourned within minutes for lack of quorum after its estranged ally, the PPP, stayed away from the proceedings over the alleged rigging in the recently-held Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) elections.

The government failed to muster the required number of 84 lawmakers in the 336-member house, forcing the chair to adjourn the session without taking up any agenda item when quorum was pointed out by an opposition member from the PTI.

“No PPP, no quorum, simple,” posted PPP’s Sharmila Farooqui on her official social media account on X soon after the adjournment of the sitting.

Later, Ms Farooqui told Dawn PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari had already declared the party would “no more cooperate with PML-N on quorum and legislation” in the parliament till their grievances over the alleged rigging and mismanagement in the AJK polls were addressed.

Sharmila says ‘no PPP, no quorum, simple’

Even those party MNAs who were present at the start of the Question Hour left the chamber immediately seeing only 20 to 25 PML-N members on the treasury benches, she said, adding that the PPP had been completing the quorum in the assembly previously.

Ms Farooqui made it clear that the strategy would not change until their concerns over the AJK polls issue were addressed. She, however, did not elaborate any specific demand when asked as to what steps the party wanted the PML-N to take in order to allay their concerns when the election process had already been completed.

When Speaker Ayaz Sadiq earlier announced the opening of the Question Hour, PTI’s Iqbal Afridi pointed out lack of quorum. His action came when the speaker refused him the floor to speak on a point of order.

The speaker ordered a headcount and suspended the proceedings till the completion of the quorum. Some 35 minutes later, Deputy Speaker Ghulam Mustafa Shah was seen in the chair when the house resumed its proceedings. He adjourned the sitting till Tuesday after finding the house still not in order due to lack of quorum.

While the PPP had supported the government in the passage of the two security-related bills last week, Mr Bhutto-Zardari, in the presence of PM Shehbaz Sharif, had objected to the manner with which the government had been doing legislation.

After developing differences with the PML-N over the issue of AJK elections, a PPP delegation headed by Mr Bhutto-Zardari called on opposition leaders and sought their cooperation on the legislation in the parliament and its committees.

Hina Javed’s murder

At the outset of the sitting, the NA speaker expressed his concerns over the brutal murder of Hina Javed in Rawalpindi and referred the matter to the relevant house committee.

Mr Sadiq disclosed that Hina Javed had been posted in the National Assembly by the National IT Board on attachment from December 2019 till June this year after which she returned to her parent department. He said though such matters generally fell under provincial jurisdiction, the case was of particular concern since she had served at the NA.

He said the manner in which Hina Javed was murdered, and the violence against women, were matters of serious concern for everyone.

He appreciated the Women Parliamentary Caucus for taking up the matter and said the NA would provide full support in monitoring the case and extending whatever assistance was required.

Minister for Law and Human Rights Azam Nazeer Tarar said the ministry was in constant contact with the Rawalpindi police regarding the murder investigations. Two suspects were on three-day physical remand, he said, expressing the confidence that the culprits would be brought to justice.

Published in Dawn, August 25th, 2026

World.title: Mission to retrieve Pakistani climber Asma Mushtaq's body from Spatnik resumes
World.content:
A rescue team resumed its trek at Spantik on Tuesday to recover the body of Pakistani mountaineer Dr Asma Mushtaq, who died while descending the 7,027m peak in Gilgit-Baltistan’s Shigar district.

The 34-year-old died at an altitude of around 6,250 metres on Aug 20, while descending from the mountain also known as Golden Peak, after suffering from high-altitude sickness. Her body remains at Camp 3.

Efforts to retrieve her body were earlier disrupted due to severe weather.

Alpine Club of Pakistan (ACP) General Secretary Ayaz Shigri told Dawn on Monday that weather conditions were expected to improve on Tuesday, after which rescuers would make another attempt to bring Mushtaq’s body down to the base camp.

Subsequently, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar posted on X that the rescue team had resumed its operation after weather conditions improved.

“The rescue team has once again departed from the base camp and is now heading towards Camp 2. The team is moving carefully and will continue the operation as conditions permit. We pray for their safety and success,” he said.

Shigri had told Dawn that Pakistan Army helicopters were expected to airlift Mushtaq’s body to Skardu after its arrival at the base camp.

During her ascent, Mushtaq had successfully reached the 7,027-metre summit of Spantik and was in good health at the time, ACP said in statements issued on Thursday.

However, she developed a serious high-altitude medical emergency at an elevation of about 6,400 metres (21,000 feet) during the descent.

High-altitude sickness encompasses a range of pulmonary and cerebral conditions caused by hypoxia, or oxygen deprivation, due to rapid ascent and inadequate acclimatisation to high altitudes.

Her mountain guide, Akbar Ali, and expedition guide, Muhammad Amin, immediately came to her assistance.

“Despite the immediate and dedicated efforts of her mountain guides, who provided every possible ass­i­s­tance under extre­mely challenging conditions, she could not survive,” Karrar Haidri, a senior vice president for ACP, said in a condolence statement.

Shigri said Mushtaq was part of a five-member Pakistani women’s expedition team that summited Spantik, which included climbers Zoni Aslam, Zaba Shigri, Shama and Sohana.

World.title: 3 more Adiala inmates seek private care
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: At least three inma­tes of Adiala jail have approached the Isla­mabad High Court seeking treatment at private hospitals and greater access to their families, following the Supreme Court’s recent order directing authorities to shift former prime minister Imran Khan to a private hospital for medical examination and treatment.

The petitions before the IHC vindicate the government’s concern that the SC order in Imran Khan’s case could set a precedent for other prisoners to seek similar relief.

The federal government, in its review petition before the Supreme Court, had argued that allowing a convict to receive treatment at a private hospital could disturb the existing prison system and trigger a “floodgate” of similar applications from other prisoners.

The issue is now before the IHC, where Justice Muhammad Asif sought comments from the jail superintendent on petitions filed by prisoners Ilyas Khan, Muhammad Ismail Khan and Owais Altaf. The court also issued noti­ces to prison authorities, and adjourned proceedings until Aug 27.

During the hearing, Barrister Akhtar Chheena, representing Ismail Khan, said his client was suffering from haemophilia and had developed internal bleeding. He submitted that the prisoner had been taken to hospital around 10 times in the last two months, but his condition had not improved.

According to the counsel, treatment for the particular condition was presently possible only at Shifa Interna­tio­nal Hospital. He relied upon the SC’s recent ruling and argued that where a disease could not be treated at a government hospital, a prisoner could be shifted to a private facility, with the family bearing the cost of treatment.

The counsel requested the court to constitute a medical board to determine whether the required treatment was available at a government hospital. He questioned whether a prisoner should be denied access to a private facility if a necessary procedure, including a liver transplant, was not available at a government hospital.

The petition filed by Owais Altaf was also pressed before Justice Muh­am­­mad Asif. His lawyer, Syed Jafar, ap­­p­eared through video link and submitted that the prisoner was suffering from fever and a heart ailment.

He argued that receiving proper medical treatment was a fundamental right of a prisoner and maintained that the required treatment was not available at a government facility. The counsel consequently sought an order for Owais Altaf’s transfer to Shifa International Hospital for treatment.

In another plea, Ismail Khan sought permission to communicate with his brother, who has been living in Dubai. The counsel requested that the jail authorities be directed to facilitate communication between the prisoner and his brother.

Published in Dawn, August 25th, 2026

World.title: Govt increases petrol price by Rs0.39, high-speed diesel by Rs2.40
World.content:
The government on Monday raised the price of petrol by Rs0.39 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs2.40 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs341.98 per litre while HSD will cost Rs370.69 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable on August 25 (Tuesday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Bitcoin rises above $80,000 as soft dollar, debasement fears boost momentum
World.content:
Bitcoin rose above $80,000 to hit a more than three-month high on Tuesday as a soft US dollar, in the wake of the moves by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to calm the bond market, revived momentum in the crypto sector.

US President Donald Trump last week called on Congress to pass a bill that would bring clearer definitions to the growing cryptocurrency sector. Since then, bitcoin, the world’s largest cryptocurrency, has risen 16 per cent.

It was last at $80,323.24 in Asian hours, having earlier touched $81,237.94, its highest level since mid-May. Bitcoin is up 28pc so far in August, set for its biggest monthly gain since November 2024.

Cryptocurrencies also got a big boost after the US Treasury last week unveiled plans to buy back more long-dated bonds to help cap the gains in the long-end yields, a move that has led to the US dollar bearing the brunt of investor angst.

Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey Group, said Bessent’s messaging has reinforced the market’s view that, at least through the midterm elections, US policymakers may have a lower tolerance for a further rise in long-end yields.

“That would create a relatively supportive macro backdrop for assets such as bitcoin and gold,” Sun said.

Gold has been the other beneficiary of the dollar weakness, rising to a three-month high.

The Treasury announcement is “exactly the type of thing bitcoin loves”, Geoff Kendrick, global head of digital assets research at Standard Chartered, said in a note last week, adding that bitcoin was built to allow investors a way to avoid this type of intervention.

The action stoked increased chatter around the so-called debasement trade, where the moves to prevent long-end yields from reaching market-clearing levels via buybacks lead the pressure to shift from the bond market to the currency market.

“This (Treasury announcement) prompted buyers to scramble into physical and digital assets as debasement trade fears re-emerged,” said Tony Sycamore, market analyst at IG.

“A sustained break above here would open the door for a move towards $95,000 and $100,000.”

World.title: Rawalpindi police chief rules out suicide in Hina Javaid’s death
World.content:
RAWALPINDI: Regional Police Officer (RPO) Babar Sarfraz Alpa has disputed the impression that Hina Javaid’s death was a suicide.

He categorically said “it was a murder”, adding her husband and a domestic servant are in police remand custody, while the father-in-law of the victim is under investigation.

The RPO was speaking at a hurriedly-called joint press conference with City Police Officer Hassan Mushtaq Sukhera, the SSP investigations and the SP Potohar at the Police Lines auditorium on Monday night.

A special team has been formed to investigate the murder of digital media executive, Hina Javaid, 45.

Says husband and servant in remand custody, father-in-law under probe

Initially, it was portrayed as a suicide; however, after examining the body, the impression of suicide was ruled out. The victim’s father-in-law has been included in the investigation but has not been arrested.

“The investigation into the case is at an early stage, so it is not appropriate to reveal certain things at this stage. However, as the investigation progresses, those who have played a role will be identified. As soon as concrete evidence is found against the victim’s father-in-law, action will be taken against him according to the law,” the RPO said.

He said that on August 20, at 6am, Asghar Ali Fayyaz came to the police station and gave the initial information that thieves had broken into his house located on Faisal Alvi Road.

He said on receiving the information, the police reached the spot where the body of Ms Javed was found in the bathroom of the apartment. “The body was tied to the shower and her hands were tied behind her back.”

On the request of the deceased’s brother Fahad Javed, a case was registered under murder charges.

The deceased’s husband Faisal Asghar Imam, father-in-law Asghar Fayyaz and domestic servant Zeeshan and an unknown person were named in the FIR.

The RPO said that the investigation was being conducted from all angles and a special team had been formed under the leadership of the SSP investigations.

He said the suspects, Zeeshan and Faisal, are in police custody. The RPO said all means, including technical and human intelligence, are being used in the investigation.

The servant revealed to the investigating team that Faisal and Hina had a quarrel on the night of the incident over some issue during which she was reportedly tortured. As she tried to escape, she was strangled, he added. Later, she was taken to the bathroom to give an impression that she had committed suicide.

The suspect had initially given a different statement but during the remand custody he made the disclosures.

Published in Dawn, August 25th, 2026

World.title: US removes Syria from state sponsor of terrorism list
World.content:
WASHINGTON: The United States on Monday delisted Syria as a state sponsor of terrorism, rescinding a decades-old designation that had severely impeded investment.

The US Department of State also revoked its designation of al-Nusrah Front — also known as Hay’at Tahrir al-Sham (HTS) — as a global terrorist organisation. The Treasury Department followed through with sanctions relief.

“Today’s action will help foster additional investment in Syria to promote political and economic stability,” Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a statement.

Treasury said the moves were “in line with President (Donald) Trump’s promise to deliver sanctions relief to Syria.” But the agency stressed that its removal of restrictions on Syria “does not change Treasury’s posture with regards to countering global terrorism and our commitment to hold bad actors in Syria accountable.”

The HTS was earlier known as Al Nusra Front and was formerly the branch of Al Qaeda in Syria. But it broke ties with the group in 2016 and sought to soften its image.

The United States had initially announced in July its intent to delist Syria as a sponsor of terrorism, a move seen as a vote of confidence in Ahmed al-Sharaa.

Published in Dawn, August 25th, 2026

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The third and unidentified accused was on the run. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded Sohel's confessional statement after police brought him to the magistrate’s chamber, said a court staff member.

Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that day, the prime accused had already admitted to the crime during primary interrogation.

On May 22, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal assistance to the accused following an emergency virtual meeting of its executive committee, citing the gravity of the allegations.

The next day, the government appointed Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah as a state defence counsel to represent the accused to ensure a fair trial.

This report has been corrected at 4:43pm. In the earlier version, Sohel Rana’s comment was misreported. We regret the error.

World.title: Why Bangladesh must pivot to renewable energy now
World.content:
There are moments in a nation’s history when a crisis does more than create hardship. It reveals the weakness of an old system and opens the door to a better one. Bangladesh is now standing at such a moment.

The country is facing an energy crisis that no longer centres on power cuts. It is affecting factories, farms, schools, offices, exports, foreign currency reserves, and the daily life of ordinary people. What we are seeing today is not just a temporary shortage of gas or fuel. It is a signal that our energy system has become too dependent on imported fossil fuels.

More than 60 percent of Bangladesh’s energy demand is met through imports. LNG, coal, oil, and other fossil fuels have kept the country running for years, but this dependence has become risky and expensive. Global fuel markets are unstable because of geopolitical tension, supply chain disruption, and price volatility. For a country like Bangladesh, this creates double pressure: fuel supply becomes uncertain while fuel costs keep rising.

The government is now spending more than BDT 200 crore per day in energy subsidies. Annual energy import expenditure remains around USD 12 billion, putting serious pressure on foreign currency reserves. Nearly 70 percent of Bangladesh’s LNG imports come from Qatar. If supply is disrupted, Bangladesh can quickly face a severe shortage. In the power sector, daily gas demand exceeds 2,500 mmcfd, but supply sometimes falls to 850–900 mmcfd. This can create a power generation shortfall of 1,500–1,800 MW. Overall, the daily gas shortage exceeds 1,100 mmcfd, and peak-time electricity shortages may reach nearly 2,000 MW.

Bangladesh also has a weak Strategic Petroleum Reserve. The current reserve capacity is sufficient for only about 35–40 days, well below that of countries such as China and Japan. This makes the national energy system even more vulnerable.

Visual: Teeni and Tuni

The impact is already visible. In the readymade garments sector, gas shortages and load shedding are reducing productivity by 25–30 percent in many cases. This threatens export earnings, foreign currency reserves, and economic stability. The crisis has also reached ordinary households. Although Bangladesh declared 100 percent electrification in 2022, many rural areas still experience 10 to 20 hours of load shedding every day during summer. This affects education, small businesses, agriculture, and people’s dignity.

We have also seen long lines at fuel stations, schools moving online, and offices shortening working hours because of fuel shortages. These are not isolated events. They show how deeply energy insecurity can disturb national life.

Over the last 15 years, electricity tariffs in Bangladesh have been increased on many occasions, including more than 10 rounds of increases at both bulk and retail levels. This path is not sustainable. Fossil-fuel-based electricity depends on imported fuel, global prices, the availability of the dollar, subsidies, and repeated tariff adjustments. Solar power offers a different path. With a one-time investment, solar can provide stable energy for 15–20 years. Once installed, its fuel cost is almost zero.

The economic comparison is clear. A 1 MW HFO-based power plant produces electricity per year at a cost of nearly BDT 190 crore, with much of the cost paid in foreign currency. In contrast, a 5 MW solar project requires a one-time investment of around BDT 25 crore, after which fuel costs are practically zero. Each 1 MW of solar power can save around USD 325,000 per year in foreign currency.

This is why renewable energy should not be discussed solely in technical terms like decarbonisation, emissions, and sustainability. For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Despite Bangladesh’s potential, renewable energy contributes less than 5 percent to power generation, far below the global 30 percent target by 2030. Clear, measurable goals and timelines are essential for effective policy planning and investment decisions.
